title: Germany – Architectural, construction, engineering and inspection services – Zweiphasiger städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Wettbewerb nach RPW 2013 - Produktives Quartier Gutleut-West
description: Gegenstand des Wettbewerbes ist ein städtebaulich-freiraumplanerischer Entwurf in dem gezeigt wird, wie die Transformation eines gewerblich geprägten Bestandsareals zu einem nutzungsgemischten, klimaangepassten und gemeinwohlorientierten Quartier gelingen kann. In einer Stadt mit hoher Flächennachfrage und begrenzten innerstädtischen Entwicklungsreserven treffen hier Ansprüche unmittelbar aufeinander, die sich andernorts oft räumlich aus dem Weg gehen: Wohnen und Gewerbe, Logistik und Aufenthalt, soziale Infrastruktur und Produktion, Freiraum und Verdichtung. Die entscheidende Frage lautet deshalb nicht, welche Nutzung sich am Ende durchsetzt. Interessanter ist, wie aus dieser Konkurrenz ein Stück Stadt entstehen kann. Aufgabe des Wettbewerbs ist es, eine eigene räumliche Antwort zu entwickeln. Gesucht wird vornehmlich nicht das möglichst vollständige Bild eines irgendwann „fertigen“ Gutleut-West. Gesucht wird vielmehr ein städtebauliches und freiraumplanerisches Gerüst, das Orientierung gibt, ohne Entwicklung einzuschränken. Es soll durch zu entwickelnde Prinzipien Qualitäten sichern und zugleich Spielräume eröffnen – für unterschiedliche Nutzungen, Träger:innen, Eigentümer:innen und Entwicklungszeitpunkte. Die Ausloberin beabsichtigt, unter Würdigung der Empfehlung des Preisgerichts, das mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichnete Team mit der Ausarbeitung des Wettbewerbsergebnisses zu beauftragen. Die Ausloberin wird hierzu ein Verhandlungsverfahren ohne Teilnahmewettbewerb gemäß § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 VgV durchführen. Dabei behält sich die Ausloberin vor, das Verhandlungsverfahren zunächst nur mit dem mit dem 1. Preis ausgezeichneten Team durchzuführen. Scheitern diese Verhandlungen oder besteht ein wichtiger Grund, der einer Beauftragung des 1. Preisträgers entgegensteht, werden die weiteren Preisträger zur Teilnahme an den Verhandlungen aufgefordert. Das Wettbewerbsergebnis wird im anschließenden Vergabeverfahren als Zuschlagskriterium mit 60 % gewichtet. Die Rangfolge der Preisträger gemäß der Entscheidung des Preisgerichts wird dabei entsprechend berücksichtigt, d.h. der 1. Preisträger erhält im Kriterium ‚Wettbewerbsergebnis' die höchste Punktzahl, der 2. Preisträger die zweithöchste usw. Die weitere Bearbeitung umfasst den städtebaulichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 51 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie den freiräumlichen Entwurf nach Merkblatt Nr. 52 der Architektenkammer Baden-Württemberg, Honorarzone IV, Leistungsphasen 1–3 sowie die Erstellung eines "Qualitätshandbuchs". Eine darüberhinausgehende Beauftragung weiterer Planungsleistungen bleibt vorbehalten und ist nicht Bestandteil dieses Auftragsversprechens. Ziel ist die Erarbeitung eines Rahmenplans mit integrierter Freiraumplanung als Vorstufe zum Bebauungsplan nach BauGB sowie als Grundlage für das im Anschluss geplante Konzeptverfahren für die hochbauliche Entwicklung auf den Baufeldern. Die Preisträger:innen verpflichten sich, im Falle einer Beauftragung durch die Ausloberin, die weitere Bearbeitung zu übernehmen und durchzuführen. Im Zuge der Überarbeitung der Wettbewerbsergebnisse treten sie mit der Bürgerschaft und Schlüsselpersonen vor Ort im Rahmen von Dialogformaten in Austausch (z.B. Vorstellung des Wettbewerbs-Ergebnisses, Rückfragenbeantwortung, Aufnahme von Hinweisen für weitere Bearbeitung). Die Beauftragung erfolgt vorbehaltlich des Abschlusses des erforderlichen Vergabeverfahrens, der erforderlichen haushaltsrechtlichen Voraussetzungen, der Eignung des Teilnehmers sowie des Vorliegens eines wichtigen Grundes, der einer Beauftragung entgegensteht. Im Falle einer weiteren Bearbeitung werden durch den Wettbewerb bereits erbrachte Leistungen des Preisträgers bis zur Höhe des zuerkannten Preises nicht erneut vergütet, wenn und soweit der Wettbewerbsentwurf unverändert der weiteren Bearbeitung zugrunde gelegt wird.

title: Germany – Landscape gardening services – Konzeption, Ausschreibung und Überwachung naturschutzfachlicher Landschaftspflege
description: Im Landschaftspark Johannisthal wurden Ausgleichsflächen für Trockenrasen, Zauneidechsen und Brutvögel angelegt, die durch naturschutzfachliche Pflege zu entwickeln sind. Leistungsgegenstand sind u.a. die Erstellung von Ausschreibungsunterlagen für die Pflegeleistungen für die Jahre 2027 bis 2028 und ab 2029 sowie die Pflegeüberwachung/-steuerung in enger Abstimmung mit dem AG, den beteiligten Behörden und den Fachbüros für das Monitoring zum Biotop- bzw. Artenschutz. Diese Ausschreibung richtet sich an Büros der Landschaftsplanung/-architektur/-ökologie und vergleichbare Berufsgruppen, die betreffend der lokaltypischen Grünlandvegetation besondere floristische und ökologische Kenntnisse nachweisen können (u.a. zu Brache- und Störzeigern, problematischen Neophyten und deren Standortansprüchen, Ansprache auch zu unterschiedlichen phänologischen Zuständen). Weiterhin sind einschlägige Erfahrung in der Bau- und Pflegeüberwachung von Landschaftsbauarbeiten erforderlich.

title: Solid-State Energy Conversion from Heat to Electricity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is requesting information on the current state of the art and technological limitations of solid-state direct thermal-to-electric energy conversion technologies. We define solid state energy conversion as systems that convert a temperature differential directly into electrical energy without utilizing mechanical moving parts (e.g., pistons, turbines, or rotary alternators). This RFI seeks to identify the best possible solid state heat engine performance across a wide operating temperature range, factors that limit performance, and the most attractive use cases if these highly efficient solid state heat engines could be made today. This survey of limits, challenges and use cases will identify opportunities for research and development to inform potential program(s) in this area.

title: Ireland – Real estate agency services on a fee or contract basis – Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks for Public Transport, Roads, Greenways and Active Travel Projects
description: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) intends to establish four-year multi-supplier Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks (Lot 1 and 2) to provide a broad range of property, valuation, land acquisition, compensation, estate management, development, regeneration, and related advisory services in support of its infrastructure programmes and corporate property requirements. This competition will comprise of two lots: Lot 1 – Public Transport and Corporate Services This Lot will provide multi-disciplinary real estate consultancy services to support TII's public transport programmes and corporate property portfolio. Public transport projects include light rail, metro and other transport infrastructure projects delivered by TII under its remit from the National Transport Authority. The Framework will be available to TII and any statutory delivery body established for the delivery of MetroLink. Key services include: Property acquisition, disposal and leasing Valuation and compensation advice CPO support services Property negotiations and stakeholder engagement Estate and asset management Development and regeneration advice Rating and taxation services Facilities management Expert witness and dispute resolution services Planning, environmental and specialist property advisory services Estimated value: €12.5 million to €15.75 million. Lot 2 – Major and Minor Roads, Greenways and Active Travel This lot will support the planning and delivery of roads, greenway and active travel projects nationwide and will be available to both TII and Local Authorities. Key services include: Land and property valuation Land acquisition and compensation Agricultural and agronomy advice Accommodation works assessments Wayleave and rights-of-way acquisition Stakeholder and landowner negotiations Land cost estimation and risk assessment CPO support and compensation claim management Arbitration and expert witness services Mapping, land transfer and close-out reporting Estimated value: €9.1 million to €12 million.

title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil) ====A0001==== This amendment formally establishes the deadline for receipt of industry questions. All questions must be submitted no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 1000 Hours MT. Questions with answers will be posted Tuesday, November 10, 2026 by 1000 Hours MT. ====A0001====

title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project as the Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 11 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. title: Float Well Pipe Repairs, Surry Mountain Dam, Surry, NH
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, New England District is issuing this Sources Sought Announcement for Construction Services for the for the repairing of the inlet pipe to the float well and replace weathered/damaged staff gauges at the Surry Moutain Lake Dam in Surry NH. This announcement is to determine interest, availability and capability of 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned and Small Business concerns for this project. The NAICS code for this procurement is 237990 with a size standard of $45M. The project is planned to be solicited in the Winter of 2026 with construction to begin place in the Summer of 2027. The estimated construction cost is between $350,000 - $500,000. The project site is the inlet culvert on the lake side of the Surry Mountain Dam in Surry, NH. Work for this project will likely include, but not be limited to, the following: Coffer dam at inlet pipe location. Float well pipe (3-inch cast iron) cleaning. Installation of internal liner for float well pipe. Pre and Post liner installation CCTV inspections. Repairs to the slash-zone pipe segment Protection and concrete encasement of the external float well pipe Staff Gauges: Pressure treated posts with attached enamel coated metal measuring strip. Scheduled work will be affected by depth of pool. Assumed low pool depths are July and August (when work can be conducted safely), but adverse weather conditions (rain events) could delay or postpone work schedules. Surry Mountain staff will keep COR informed of pool levels to anticipate when work can commence if outside assumed low pool depths. Interested firms should submit a capabilities package to include the following: business classification (i.e. HUBZone, small business, etc.), as well as qualifications and experience in performing the work components stated above. Please include at least two specific examples of the firm�s experience performing the work requirements stated above. The projects must have been performed within the last seven years. Please indicate the team subcontractor(s) (if any), including their prior experience and qualifications, which will be used to support the offeror�s effort, and their experience must also have been performed within the last seven years. Proof of bonding capability is required. Responses are limited to twenty pages. Responses are due by 21 September 2026. Responses should be emailed to: Kyle Hall � kyle.k.hall@usace.army.mil Phone Contact: (978) 318-8479 Interested firms shall provide the above documentation in one original form and one copy. The Government will not pay for any material provided in response to this market survey nor return the data provided. This notice is for information purposes only and is not a request to be placed on a solicitation mailing list nor is it a Request for Proposal (RFP) or an announcement of a solicitation. The results of this survey will be considered to be in effect for a period of one year from the date of this notice. title: INL Serbia Shooting Range Simulator System
description: The International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Section of the Embassy of the United States of America in Serbia supports procurement of a scenario-based laser shooting range system and complementary tactical preparedness and response police training kits to complete new training facilities at University or Criminal Investigation and Police Studies in Belgrade, Serbia. This training solution will provide controlled, analytical training environment needed to assess, document, and translate scenario-based tactical instruction into measurable performance improvements, institutional accountability and long-term learning. SUBSTANTIVE REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall fulfill the following substantive requirements (See Attachment A RFQ/SOW for a complete listing of requirements/quantities): I LASER TRAINING SIMULATOR SYSTEM II SIMULATION TRAINING CENTRE - TRAINING KITS III INSTALLATION/TRAINING � ONSITE INTERNATIONAL Delivery The vendor is responsible for the delivery of all items. The vendor shall consolidate the entire shipment to prevent loss and misdirection. Entire shipment must be consolidated at the origin and shipped consolidated, partial shipments are not accepted by post due to the Serbian customs donation regulations. Entire shipment must be consolidated under one AWB or CMR. Any lost or damaged items during shipment shall be replaced by the contractor upon notification. Packaging and preservation shall be IAW best commercial practices to enable shipment to final destination in Serbia to the address specified (see Attachment A RFQ/SOW), without repacking or incurring damage during shipment and handling. Delivery shall be made FOB Destination as soon as possible but not later than 90 days from the date of contract award. Submission Requirements (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) Evaluation Criteria (please see details in the Attachment A � RFQ/SOW) After initial evaluation of quotes, the Contracting Officer may negotiate final terms with one or more contractors of the Government�s choice before issuing a purchase order. The Contracting Officer will not negotiate with any contractors other than those of the Government�s choice and will not use the formal source selection procedures described in FAR Part 15. The Government may perform a comparative evaluation to select the contractor that provides the best value, considering the evaluation factors below. The Contracting Officer may issue a purchase order to other than the contractor with the lowest proposed price. The Government will consider the following factors when selecting contractors for award. The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotes: 1) Technical Specifications: Quote must meet or exceed required technical specifications. Compliance with all required features (to include realism of the training, system flexibility, and performance-measurement tools). Quote meets warranty term requirements. Quote verifies compliance with all requested equipment/quantities, utilizing Exhibit A, �Technical Specs�. 2) Delivery Timeline. 3) International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe: The entity demonstrating International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe. 4) Past Performance: The entity demonstrates relevant past performance in at least three (3) contracts of similar or superior characteristics to those of this project. 5) Price: The overall price will be considered, and the lowest price is favorable.

title: Remediation and Restoration Activities
description: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�, -74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Additional components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. An outline summarizing the required content of the work plan is Technical Approach (Method and procedures for soil remediation, removal, disposal a. Identification of required work permits and b. Site Safety Health Plan (SSHP). Risk Management Plan a. Identification of major risks and b.Risk mitigation plan. The contractor should expect a 5-business day Volpe Center review period between submission of the Draft Work Plan and receipt of Volpe Center comments. The Volpe Center and the Contractor shall meet to discuss any comments and changes, if necessary. The contractor shall make the changes and submit a Final Work Plan within 5 business days of the receipt of comments. Contaminated Soil Remediation: Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation (PA/SI) and Remedial Investigation (RI) activities completed between 2020 and 2025 found soils at the below site containing contamination above FAA�s action levels, which are based on U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and/or New Jersey Residential Soil Remediation Standards. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. title: FDA Scientific & Regulatory Support Services(SRS)
description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Instructions for Responses: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions). The anticipated period of performance is a 5-year ordering period. After review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). Responses to this notice must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (Attachment A). All interested parties can provide written opinions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Business Status Provide the legal business name and address Primary point of contact and the contact information SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE code Proposed NAICS code and size status Applicable small-business socioeconomic designations (including 8(a), HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, veteran-owned, women-owned, or small disadvantaged business, as applicable) Identify whether the respondent proposes to participate as prime contractor, joint venture, or subcontractor Responses to this notice shall be submitted via e-mail to Amanda Edger, Contract Specialist, at Amanda.Edger@fda.hhs.gov (with a CC: to Ian Weiss, Contracting Officer, at Ian.Weiss@fda.hhs.gov), by November 19, 2026, at 2:00 pm. After a review of the received responses, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation. title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: **AMMENDMENT 1. REMOVED INCORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION AND UPLOADED CORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION*** The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. The contractor will be required to provide these services on an estimated two to three month interval between the hours of 7:30AM-3:00PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The exact intervals between cleanings will be determined as needed by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). FCI McKean has one 10,000 gallon trap within the secure confines behind the Food Service department, and one 2,000 gallon trap at the satellite prison camp. All grease and pumpings removed shall be disposed of in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The contractor shall furnish an invoice for each service delivered at the time of extraction. All extractions and cleanings will be verified and signed for by an authorized representative. Specific Requirements The contractor will be licensed/permitted by the State of Pennsylvania and will provide evidence of proper waste disposal, in accordance with all current Federal, State, and local codes, laws, and requirements regarding the disposal of solid waste. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.

description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Objectives: The objective of the contemplated SRS acquisition is to provide FDA with responsive, high-quality scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the task order, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and nonclinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. The Government is interested in sources capable of providing the scientific depth and operational capacity needed to: Conduct scientifically sound analyses and prepare defensible, traceable technical products supporting FDA review and public-health decisions. Provide qualified personnel across multiple scientific and regulatory disciplines, including specialized and emerging areas. Support clinical and nonclinical study-data review, standardized scientific datasets, statistical computing, data fitness, quality assessment, and interpretation. Respond to multiple simultaneous task orders, changing priorities, time-sensitive scientific questions, and evolving requirements across FDA organizations. Maintain scientific quality, data integrity, documentation, confidentiality, and continuity of performance. Deliver effective scientific training, technical writing, knowledge transfer, and program-management support tied directly to scientific and regulatory missions. Project Requirements: The following descriptions are illustrative of the types of services that may be ordered. They are provided to inform industry responses and do not establish final task-order requirements. Each task order would define its own objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance expectations, staffing qualifications, and period of performance. Scientific Research and Regulatory Review Support: Support scientific investigations, literature and evidence reviews, research planning, study design, methodological assessments, scientific consultations, and technical analyses relevant to FDA-regulated products. Prepare scientific assessments, briefing materials, review support documentation, and other products that allow Government scientists and reviewers to evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings. Provide subject-matter expertise to address complex or emerging regulatory science questions. Clinical and Nonclinical Study-Data Review and Analysis: Support the scientific review of clinical and nonclinical datasets submitted for regulatory purposes, including data fitness and completeness assessments, exploratory safety analyses, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, listings, figures, and visualizations. Experience with standards such as CDISC SDTM, ADaM, and SEND may be relevant. The RRS BPA describes review-oriented services that assess study data and produce analyses for FDA reviewers; SRS would focus on the scientific and analytical performance of those services rather than maintenance of the underlying software platforms. Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Pharmacovigilance, and Surveillance: Conduct epidemiological and Pharmacoepidemiological research, biostatistical analyses, pharmacovigilance assessments, signal detection and evaluation, public-health surveillance, and interpretation of real-world data and evidence as required by individual scientific programs. Activities may include protocol and analysis-plan support, assessment of study limitations and bias, statistical programming, results interpretation, and technical reporting. Scientific Data Standards, Quality, and Analytics: Provide scientific expertise related to data standards, controlled terminology, study-data interpretation, data quality and fitness, and reproducible analytical methods. Support scientific data preparation and validation, biostatistics, bioinformatics, computational science, and other specialized analyses when the primary deliverable is scientific or regulatory in nature. Distinguish these activities from enterprise database administration, application development, platform engineering, and IT operations. Laboratory and Specialized Scientific Support: Provide laboratory-related scientific and technical expertise, research assistance, analytical method support, study coordination, quality documentation, and interpretation or reporting of laboratory findings where required by a task order. Respondents should identify the specific laboratory disciplines, facilities, qualifications, and methods they can support rather than assume that all clinical trial operations

title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. HARS sampling and testing would adhere to the procedures, and their subsequent updates, as described in: 2016 US Army Corps of Engineers New York District/EPA Region 2 Guidance for Performing Tests on Dredged Material Proposed for Ocean Disposal (a.k.a. Regional Testing Manual) (http://www.nan.usace.army.mil/Portals/37/docs/regulatory/Formdoc/FINAL_NYD-R2_REGIONAL_TESTINGMANUAL-APRIL%202016.pdf) 1991 EPA/USACE, Evaluation of Dredged Material Proposed for Ocean Disposal (a.k.a. the Green Book) (https://www.epa.gov/sites/production/files/2015-10/documents/green_book.pdf). The IDIQ contract would also include the sampling and testing of dredged material proposed for upland placement. �Upland� sampling and testing would adhere to the procedures, and their subsequent updates, as described in: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) New Jersey Administrative Code (NJAC), Title 7, Chapters 9 and 26 (a.k.a. �NJAC 7�) (https://dep.nj.gov/rules/current-rules-and-regulations/) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) manual, entitled �Technical & Operational Guidance Series (TOGS) 5.1.9 In-Water and Riparian Management of Sediment and Dredged Material� (November 2004) (a.k.a. �TOGS 5.1.9�) (https://www.dec.ny.gov/docs/water_pdf/togs519.pdf) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, New York Codes, Rules and Regulations (NYCRR), Title 6, Part 375 (December 2025) (a.k.a. �6 NYCRR Part 375�) (https://dec.ny.gov/sites/default/files/2025-12/6nycrrpart375final.pdf). Other state procedures may also be requested and would be coordinated between NYD and the contractor to determine capabilities. Additional work under this contract will include analyses of sediment, tissue, and water and may include environmental DNA/metagenomic analyses related to HARS monitoring in accordance with the following document and any subsequent updates: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) New York District and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2, Site Management and Monitoring Plan for Historic Area Remediation Site (HARS) (July 2020). Task orders would include all or some of the following: sediment and water collection (on Contractor-supplied ship) handling, processing and shipping of samples physical and chemical analyses quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) procedures, and necessary corrective actions. For each task order, the contractor would provide reports containing the sampling logs, all testing results and QA/QC information in the format required by NYD, EPA � Region 2, and/or state agencies. In addition to sampling and testing for ocean placement, NYD also requires that contractors be capable of performing testing procedures such as the Synthetic Precipitation Leaching Procedure (SPLP), the Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP), and the Modified Elutriate Test (MET), which are required for upland placement of dredged material in the states of New York and New Jersey. Prior to sampling and testing, a Work/Quality Assurance (QA) Plan and an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) would need to be prepared by the contractor and approved by NYD. A Work/QA Plan must include: descriptions of all technical procedures for field sampling, laboratory analyses (e.g. biological, physical) for HARS and upland testing, data reduction and validation, and reporting clearly written standard operating procedures (SOP) for all field, experimental and analytical procedures clearly defined QA objectives that are consistent with the regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) and if applicable, permit application mechanisms for conducting performance and systems audits during the course of the field laboratory work procedures for detecting problems with sampling and analytical work, and implementation of corrective actions in a timely manner. All sampling would be performed within the Port of New York & New Jersey, all Federal Navigation Channels within New York District, the length of the Hudson River, in the Atlantic Ocean at the Historic Area Remediation Site and its Mud Dump Reference Site. �New Work or Harbor Deepening� projects may be proposed and coordinated between NYD and the contractor. A detailed description of work required for these contracts will be provided in its entirety upon issuance of the complete solicitation. Prior to issuance of the solicitation, it is highly recommended that interested parties read the required regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) in order to obtain a thorough understanding of the work required by the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The Period of Performance will be five (5) years from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The contract magnitude will be up to $10,000,000.00 for five (5) years � up to $2,000,000.00 each year. One contract will be awarded on an Unrestricted Full and Open Competition basis to the lowest bidder who has, within the last 18 months, demonstrated their capability of performing the program�s work to EPA � Region 2. A bidder can prove their capability through one of the following: the bidder has received, within the last 18 months from EPA � Region 2, documentation stating that the laboratory has submitted data that is fully acceptable or acceptable with qualification; or the bidder has satisfied the Demonstration of Capability (DOC) requirements for the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541380. The business size standard is $25,500,000.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: **AMMENDMENT 1. REMOVED INCORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION AND UPLOADED CORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION*** **AMMENDMENT 2. UPLOADED AMENDMENT DOCUMENT 15B20927Q00000001 P00001 RFQ GREASE TRAP.pdf THIS DOCUMENT UPDATES THE OPTION YEARS IN LINE ITEMS 2 THROUGH 5. TO BEGIN ON OCTOBER 1 INSTEAD OF DECEMBER. UPDATED TERMS AND CONDITIONS. ADDED 52.217-9 AND REMOVED 52.226-3. **** The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. The contractor will be required to provide these services on an estimated two to three month interval between the hours of 7:30AM-3:00PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The exact intervals between cleanings will be determined as needed by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). FCI McKean has one 10,000 gallon trap within the secure confines behind the Food Service department, and one 2,000 gallon trap at the satellite prison camp. All grease and pumpings removed shall be disposed of in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The contractor shall furnish an invoice for each service delivered at the time of extraction. All extractions and cleanings will be verified and signed for by an authorized representative. Specific Requirements The contractor will be licensed/permitted by the State of Pennsylvania and will provide evidence of proper waste disposal, in accordance with all current Federal, State, and local codes, laws, and requirements regarding the disposal of solid waste. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.

title: USCG ISA Tenant Improvement Construction Project
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. No solicitation or specifications are available at this time. Please monitor sam.gov as this Sources Sought Notice will not be linked to the solicitation. The General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery Division, is conducting market research to determine if any SDVOSB, HUB Zone, EDWOSB or 8(a) Small Business Concern has the current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform the work described herein. All interested Small Business firms should respond. This Sources Sought Notice is being issued by the General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery for tenant fit-out Construction services for the United States Coast Guard (USCG) Northeast District to support mission-critical operations across the Northeast maritime region. The place of performance will be the John F. Kennedy (JFK) Federal Building (FB), located at 15 New Sudbury St, Boston, MA 02203. This is a Repair and Alteration (R&A) project which includes operational, administrative, secure, forensic, and mission-support spaces, with construction of a specialized Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) being a particularly important element.
