title: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration at NSB Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO RENOVATE THE UNACCOMPANIED ENLISTED PERSONNEL HOUSING QUARTERS (BUILDINGS 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 AND 1054) LOCATED AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE (SUBBASE) KINGS BAY, GA. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RUPHR. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) to gain knowledge of ALL qualified and interested parties. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The Government may use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: This project will include, but is not limited to, renovate the Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing Quarters (Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 and 1054) located at Naval Submarine Base (SUBBASE), Kings Bay, Georgia. Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045 and 1046 were constructed in 1984. Building 1054 was constructed in 1989. The project scope includes upgrades to mechanical systems, fire protection, fire alarms, bathrooms, and exterior renovation. Except for Air Handling Units (AHU) in Buildings 1042, 1044 and 1046, all mechanical systems are being upgraded under this project. Mechanical system repairs include replacement of HVAC AHUs, installing Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for temperature and humidity, replacement of chilled water (CHW) piping, circulation pumps and cleaning of ductwork. Plumbing repairs include the replacement of plumbing fixtures, domestic water piping and sanitary piping. Electrical system repairs include replacement of electrical service panels throughout the building. Electrical repairs also include replacement of lighting fixtures with LED fixtures and replacement of wiring and wiring devices where they do not meet the current codes. Exterior renovation includes replacement of gutters, windows, doors, safety railings, lights. Interior renovation includes remodeling of bathrooms, mold remediation, and cleaning and painting of all previously painted surfaces. Ceilings and non-loadbearing walls will be demolished and rebuilt as required to allow access to rebuild mechanical and plumbing ductwork and pipes. The project also requires the design for abatement of hazardous material. The hazardous materials survey has been conducted by the industrial hygiene professionals, and the findings of the survey are included in the report. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 1200 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. The anticipated award date is fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this Sources Sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-7). Complete submission package shall not exceed 6 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) if applicable for NAICS Code 236200 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Unique Entity Identifier. 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of three (3) to a maximum of five (5) projects demonstrating Prime construction experience demonstrating the specific capabilities listed below: Executing construction or major renovations of multi-story, multi-unit living quarters facilities including dormitories, multi-family housing, hotels, office buildings or other similar types of construction. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at $20 million or greater and/or 30,000 square feet or greater. Completed within the past seven (7) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including contract number, project title, completion date, performance ratings, and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. Please respond to this announcement no later than 23 NOV 2026, 2:00 PM Eastern Time via email to Darrien Thomas at darrien.a.thomas.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration, NSB Kings Bay. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

This notice does not constitute a solicitation, nor does it commit the Government to issue a solicitation or award a contract. The Government will not reimburse any costs associated with participation in this event. 1. Agency and Location Department of Justice Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) 400 First Street NW Washington, DC 20534 Rooms A/B/C 2. Event Description The Federal Bureau of Prisons (BOP) hereby announces an Industry Day for Tactical Protective Equipment, to be conducted December 2�3, 2026, between 8:00 AM to 3:00 PM EST each day. The purpose of this event is to obtain information from industry regarding current products, technologies, and capabilities relevant to protective tactical equipment used in correctional emergency response operations. Information obtained will support the BOP�s national contracting initiative beginning in Fiscal Year 2027. 3. Categories of Equipment for Demonstration Interested vendors shall be prepared to bring physical items for in?person demonstration. Equipment categories include, but are not limited to: � Protective helmets, including riot helmets with face shields � Riot and disturbance control shields � Shin guards and lower?leg protection � Knee and elbow pads � Tactical uniforms � Forearm and upper?arm protection � Chest, shoulder, back, and torso protection � Full?body protective suits and modular protective systems � Tactical vests (Threat Level III?A), including ballistic plate inserts � Protective gloves, including puncture?resistant products � Riot batons and associated accessories � Equipment storage, transport, and maintenance accessories � Other related protective equipment designed for correctional emergency response operations 4. Vendor Participation Requirements To participate, vendors must comply with the following: a. Equipment Transport and Restrictions � Vendors shall hand-carry or transport their equipment themselves. � No equipment shall be shipped to the BOP facility. � All items must be non?weaponized and free of ammunition, chemical agents, OC products, pyrotechnics, or operational electronic discharge devices. � Vendors are responsible for setup, handling, and removal of their own equipment. f. Facility Support and Limitations � The Government will provide tables, electricity, extension cords, and display space. � Vendors must provide their own display stands, mannequins, or mounting equipment. � Internet access will not be available. � Vendor personnel must present valid government?issued identification for facility access. 5. Purpose and Disclaimer This Industry Day is intended to enhance the Government�s understanding of current market capabilities and product availability. title: Manufacture of M284A2 155mm and other MTC Cannon Tubes
description: Purpose: The Army Contracting Command - Rock Island (ACC-RI) at Picatinny, Picatinny Arsenal, NJ 07806-5000 is conducting a Market Survey on behalf of the Project Manager Howitzer Systems (PM-HS). PM-HS has a need to identify potential sources capable of manufacturing the M284A2 155mm, and other 155mm cannon tubes domestically in specific quantities and lead time annotated below. The purpose of this market research is to obtain current information on the capability of additional sources to manufacture 155mm Cannon Tubes up to 30-foot length. No other data or drawings will be provided with this Market Survey. Description: The .39 caliber, 155-mm M776 and M284A2 cannon tubes are components of the M777A2 and M109A6/A7 Howitzers respectively. 155-mm cannons are direct support cannon fire support system for the U.S. Army and must be built to the United States Government technical data specifications. This Sources Sought is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the US Government. All interested respondents are requested to provide a written response summarizing the following capabilities and organizational details. Manufacturers with domestic capacity in the works are also encouraged submit their response along with their prospective production timetables. Please clarify if respondent�s capabilities apply to one or all the cannon tube models. REQUESTED: 1. Name of company, address, telephone number, email address, technical point of contact, CAGE code, UEI, and business size information (please specify as either a Large Business, Foreign-Owned Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, 8(a) concern, Woman-Owned Small Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone concern, Veteran-Owned Small Business, or Service-Disabled Small Business). 2. Experience: A description of the respondent�s manufacturing experience of the 155-mm Cannon Tubes, or similar products, within the last five (5) years to include past performance. Include applicable description of experience with each cannon tube. 3. Production Process: A description of the respondent�s existing 155-mm cannon production process to include all major manufacturing stages and the operations/equipment utilized for each, as well as all supporting subcontractors. The description must detail the entire production lifecycle, including, but not limited to: 3.1. A detailed description of the respondents bore and outside diameter cold working capabilities to include autofrettage. 3.2. A detailed description of the respondent�s boring and milling capabilities along with the capacity or each (length, weight, outer/inner diameters). 3.3. A detailed description of the respondent's rifling capabilities, including methods (e.g., swage, broach, or single-point machining) and general experience with standard 155-mm rifling configurations (lands, grooves, and twist rates). 3.4. A detailed description of the respondent or subcontractor coating capabilities for chrome bore coatings on a steel tube up to 30 ft long and up to 7,500 pounds in weight. Provide the maximum length and weight of tube that can be coated by respondent. 3.5. A detailed description of the respondent�s protective coating and painting capabilities. 3.6. Detailed description of the respondent�s advanced manufacturing capabilities and growth areas. 4. Production Capacity: A description of the respondent�s current maximum monthly capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes. Please specify separate production rate capacity for each and if different manufacturing lines, tooling, or subcontractors are utilized. 5. Production Availability: A description of the respondent�s maximum caliber capability and projected available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes within 18 months from the date of these sources sought. 6. Optimization opportunity: A description of the domestic facilities, equipment, machines and tooling required to increase the available capacity to produce 155-mm cannon tubes up to ten (10) tubes per month, regardless of caliber, within 36 months from the date of this source sought. Specify whether the projected production capacity for each tube type is dedicated or shared across multiple lines. Provide an NTE ROM cost estimate for an initial production quantity of forty (40) cannon tubes (broken down by caliber or indicating pricing for a combined/flexible mix). 7. Material: A detailed description of the respondent�s cannon tube source material grade, respondent(s) and processing. Such as, but not limited to, steel preform production, forging, guide bore, and heat treatment. description: ***This solicitation is a Small Business set-a-sided, restricted to 100% small business only.***The project includes repairs and upgrades to an existing fuel storage and dispensing facility. Additional work includes replacing tank vents, repairing and improving grounding systems, modifying platforms to provide safe access to tank equipment, and upgrading the automatic tank gauging (ATG) system and associated controls.*****Proposal Due Date has been extended from 11/23/2026 to 12/21/2026 at 14:00 CST*****
